question: In Postgres, how can I order rows by whichever of two date columns is earlier?
answer: Use ORDER BY least(date_one, date_two); greatest() gives the later value.
support: Simply use order by least(date_one, date_two)

question: Which company is cited as deploying to 800 servers 200 times a week using only Git, with no artifact management tool?
answer: Reddit.
support: Some places use just version control with no artifact management, i.e. Reddit. They deploy to 800 servers 200 times a week using just Git.

question: My PPTP VPN client sits behind a NAT router and a Cisco ASA, and the ASA logs a protocol 47 translation failure. What ASA config change fixed it?
answer: Add 'inspect pptp' under class inspection_default in policy-map global_policy (along with a static NAT on the Buffalo router for the wireless device).
support: policy-map global_policy class inspection_default inspect pptp

question: Why can merely opening a folder full of downloaded images be a security risk, even if you never click on a file?
answer: The file explorer automatically parses .jpg/.png files to render thumbnails, so a hole in the image library can be exploited just by opening the directory.
support: Any security hole in the JPEG or PNG support library could then be exploited by a malicious file, and it does not require any "opening click" on the file, just opening the directory.

question: Edits I make to the server's crontab keep getting overwritten every time we deploy our Rails app. What is overwriting them?
answer: The Whenever gem, which rewrites the crontab on each deploy; either remove it or use it to define the jobs.
support: This gem was overwriting the changes I made in the crontab file each time I deployed.

question: Why can't the language standard simply specify that using an address before it is allocated always causes a crash?
answer: The system's response depends on implementation, prior program actions and runtime state, so a crash may come late or never; the standard must declare behavior undefined.
support: the system response depends on details of the implementation, of the previous actions of the program, on the state of the runtime etc. in an unpredictable way.

question: How can I compute an MD5 checksum of a file while wget is still downloading it, so I don't need a second pass over the file?
answer: wget -O - http://example.com/myFile | tee myFile | md5sum > MD5SUM
support: wget -O - http://example.com/myFile | tee myFile | md5sum > MD5SUM.

question: What is the main risk of using OPTION (RECOMPILE) on queries in a production SQL Server database?
answer: Using it inappropriately, for example on high-frequency queries.
support: The main risk with OPTION(RECOMPILE) is when it's used inappropriately, such as high-frequency queries.

question: If I can't use Let's Encrypt as my certificate authority, which ACME challenge types can Ansible's generic certificate module handle?
answer: http-01, dns-01 and tls-alpn-01 challenges.
support: if you can't use letsencrypt then it might be a good tool to check out for http-01, dns-01 and tls-alpn-01 challenges.

question: What maximum loop resistance did the IEEE 802.3at-2009 PoE standard allow for cabling?
answer: 12.5 ohms, down from 20 ohms in 802.3af-2003 and later 6.25 ohms in 802.3bt-2018.
support: 802.3at-2009 lowered that to 12.5 Ω and the new 802.3bt-2018 to 6.25 Ω

question: How does an SSD's ATA Secure Erase make all data unreadable without overwriting every sector?
answer: The controller transparently encrypts all sectors with a random key; Secure Erase discards the old key and generates a new one.
support: When you run the ATA Secure Erase command, the disk controller discards the old key and generates a new one.

question: I configured an Apache virtual host for port 555 on Debian but nothing listens there. Which directive do I add to /etc/apache2/ports.conf?
answer: Listen 555
support: It should be Listen 555.

question: For a Git branching model with a separate branch per customer brand, which branch should each customer branch be created from, and how do code updates reach it?
answer: Create each customer branch from develop, then occasionally pull from develop into it (code changes on develop, asset changes on the customer branch).
support: you can create each customer branch from develop and then pull future changes in as required.

question: When malloc has no free space left inside the process, which system call does glibc ultimately use to get more memory from the kernel?
answer: The brk syscall (via the brk glibc function).
support: it (probably) calls the brk glibc function, which in turn calls the brk syscall.

question: With psql run with ON_ERROR_STOP on and --single-transaction, why is nothing rolled back when an \include file fails, and what is the workaround?
answer: ON_ERROR_STOP halts but doesn't roll back on \include error; drop --single-transaction and wrap the main script in explicit BEGIN/COMMIT.
support: removing the single-transaction option and wrapping explicit BEGIN/COMMIT statements around my main script.

question: In an AWS IAM policy limiting a user to one S3 bucket named test, what resource ARNs go with the object actions versus the list action?
answer: arn:aws:s3:::test/* for PutObject, GetObject and DeleteObject; arn:aws:s3:::test for s3:ListBucket.
support: "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::test/*"]

question: Why did replacing an old HP 1910 switch with a newer one, linked by two cables to an unmanaged 1410, make the LAN unusable?
answer: The new switch had STP off by default, so a bridge loop formed and the broadcast storm brought the network down.
support: If you replace the 1910 with a switch without STP, a bridge loop forms, causing a broadcast storm to bring down the network.

question: How many possible passwords are there for a 6-character case-insensitive alphabet-only password compared with a case-sensitive one?
answer: About 2^28 for case-insensitive versus 2^34 for case-sensitive.
support: A 6 non case sensitive character alphabet only password has 2^28 possible passwords,while a 6 character case sensitive password has 2^34 possible passwords.

question: What command imports an Oracle dmp file from an existing user's schema into a new user?
answer: imp system/password@sid file=(filename) log=imp.log fromuser=(existing user) touser=(new user)
support: imp system/password@sid file=(filename) log=imp.log fromuser=(existing user) touser=(new user)

question: In programming, what does the testing surface of an object refer to?
answer: The collective area of its public properties, methods and constructors (its API), a proxy for how much effort is needed to unit test it.
support: The testing surface of an object is the collective area that is encompassed by the public properties, methods and constructors of that object
